text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yes, hello, yes. Sorry, I was just, erm, the volume. I'm Hetal.
A: Hetal. I'm Abena. Nice to meet you.
B: Nice to meet you also.
A: Well. That puzzle at the beginning. Did you get on with it?
B: Erm, I think okay? I was a bit slow. I was worried about the time, you know.
A: I think we all were. I took a while over it myself.
B: Okay. That's good. Sorry, I mean, it's good it's not only me.
A: (laughs) No, not only you. Erm, I noticed in your picture you have a sewing machine behind you, and all the fabric. Do you sew?
B: Yes, yes. I am a tailor, alterations. Hems, zips, taking in, blouses for saris. I did it nine years at a shop in Wembley, a dry cleaner's with an alterations counter. But the shop closed, erm, about one and a half years ago. So now I'm looking for work. I do some for neighbours, for people at the temple. Like yesterday I took up three school trousers for my neighbour.
A: I'm sorry about the shop. That must have been hard, after nine years.
B: Yes, it was. It's okay. I'm applying, department stores, costume places. Sorry, my English, I'm not explaining very well.
A: Your English is perfectly fine. Honestly. You've explained it very clearly.
B: Thank you. What do you do? Your room looks so, erm, so nice. Very tidy.
A: Thank you. Well, I'm an interior design consultant. Part-time, for a small studio in Dulwich. So I meet clients, do mood boards, and I source fabrics and furniture. So, sort of, I spend a lot of time with fabric too, but from the other side, you know. I choose it, and someone like you makes it work.
B: Oh, that's nice. So you choose the curtains, the cushions?
A: Curtains, upholstery, all of that. And I'll tell you something. The person who makes the curtains matters far more than the client ever realises. A good workroom, someone who notices a few millimetres, that's everything.
B: Yes! That is me. I always see if the hem is two millimetres off. My manager used to laugh.
A: Well, that's exactly what workrooms want. Have you thought about soft furnishings? Curtain workrooms, upholstery? They're often looking for careful people.
B: Erm, no, I didn't think. I only think of clothes. Is it very different?
A: Different scale, bigger pieces, but the same care. Let me think... there are a couple of workrooms in South London we use. I can't promise anything, but it might be worth looking at that kind of place.
B: Thank you, that's very kind. I will look. I will write it down.
A: And your top, the embroidery at the neck. Did you do that?
B: Yes, I made this kurti. The embroidery also, by hand. Sorry, it's very simple.
A: It's not simple at all. It's lovely. I did fine art before design, back in Kumasi, so I notice these things.
B: Oh, you are from Ghana?
A: Accra, originally. I've been here a long time now. And you?
B: Vadodara, Gujarat. I came at twenty-two. The fabrics in Ghana, the kente, it's very beautiful. I see it on Instagram.
A: Oh, it is. My mother still has —
